ai_infrastructure.headline: Servers & Racks leads the AI stack, paced by SMCI, DELL.
ai_infrastructure.action: Start with Servers & Racks. Confirmation test: A sustained move should pull networking, cooling, power, and component suppliers higher.
ai_infrastructure.avoid: Do not treat the whole AI basket as one trade: Power & Cooling is the current weak link (-3.94% average).

sectors.label: Servers & Racks
sectors.why: Server and rack vendors show when chip demand is turning into deployable systems.
sectors.readthrough: A sustained move should pull networking, cooling, power, and component suppliers higher.

sectors.label: Networking & Optics
sectors.why: Large clusters need switches, interconnect, and optics to scale useful compute.
sectors.readthrough: Leadership confirms spend is shifting from isolated accelerators toward complete clusters.

sectors.label: Memory & Storage
sectors.why: HBM, DRAM, and storage content rise as AI servers become larger and denser.
sectors.readthrough: Sustained leadership implies the AI server bill of materials is broadening beyond GPUs.

sectors.label: Hyperscalers
sectors.why: The largest cloud platforms fund the capex cycle and turn AI demand into recurring revenue.
sectors.readthrough: Cloud growth, AI revenue, capex guidance, and free-cash-flow absorption decide durability.

sectors.label: AI Chips
sectors.why: Accelerators and silicon determine how much AI compute can be deployed.
sectors.readthrough: Strength should confirm in foundries, memory, networking, and server orders.

sectors.label: Foundries & Fab
sectors.why: Foundry utilization and equipment demand confirm whether chip demand is becoming real capacity spend.
sectors.readthrough: Watch equipment orders, advanced packaging, and memory capex for confirmation.

sectors.label: Data Centers

sectors.label: Neoclouds
sectors.why: Specialist GPU clouds are the high-beta expression of rented AI compute demand.
